comments.author: @ChandrasekharIES
comments.text:
Sir, since I work in electrical department I would like to clarify few things. 
1. The unit charge of power is combination of fixed and running cost ( for hydro running cost is less ). So direct linking construction cost with unit charge is not technically correct.
2. Hydro plants are must run plants, means they are scheduled ahead of other plants to supply power= demand for hydro plant power is always there. 
3.  Many coal based plants are running with low capacity or under reserve shutdown due to lack of coal.
4. It is the time taken to get approvals and completion time + initial cost chocks the idea of hydro plants. Now there was rise in solar plants distributed across loads.
